problem: Zero-shot open-vocabulary ObjectNav pipelines use separate encoders for frontier scoring and target confirmation, which is redundant and slow. Their confirmation is one-shot or score-averaged, so it cannot separate true targets from visually similar distractors, and frontier selection ignores expected information gain versus traversal cost.
motivation: A high detection score can mean a genuine target, a look-alike distractor, or a transient false positive, so reliable stopping needs accumulated evidence. Under weak semantic cues, agents oscillate among distant low-yield frontiers. Redundant per-step multi-model inference also creates latency that limits real-robot use.
key_idea: Treat ZSON as evidence-driven perception-to-decision: one shared C-RADIOv4 encoder with gated SAM3 segmentation, cluster-level additive log-odds beliefs with confuser and miss evidence, and frontier selection that trades off semantic value, en-route information gain, and traversal cost.
insight: Accumulating evidence is the largest contributor: removing consolidation drops SR from 84.7 to 71.9, and goal-only log-odds already reaches 81.9. Confuser evidence and miss evidence each add gains (+1.8 and +1.3 SR) and are nearly additive. The shared encoder improves accuracy (75.9 to 84.7 SR) as well as speed, and the gate skips 62.5% of SAM3 calls with no accuracy loss. Information gain helps only when paired with the traversal-cost term; alone it gives no benefit (81.9 vs 81.8 SR).
method: Evidence-gated perception: a single C-RADIOv4 forward pass gives a summary token (scene similarity to the SigLIP2 goal embedding, projected to a top-down value map) and patch tokens; SAM3 is run on shared features only if max patch similarity exceeds tau_gate=0.08
Cluster association: SAM3 instances are back-projected with depth to 3D point clouds and fused into a cluster within 0.75 m, otherwise a new cluster starts with log-odds 0

Semantic log-odds update: SAM3 is prompted with the goal and up to 3 LLM-generated confuser categories (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, cached offline); the belief goes up by logit of the goal score when the goal dominates by margin delta and down by logit of the confuser score when the confuser dominates, weighted by overlap rho_k, clamped to [-4,4]
Miss evidence: a positive-belief cluster inside the view frustum but not detected receives a negative update proportional to its visibility fraction, with prior miss rate 0.2083
Stopping rule: after the belief exceeds tau_stop=1.0 the robot approaches the cluster and stops only if this holds in at least 2 of 5 consecutive frames and it is within 0.5 m

Active evidence acquisition: frontier utility = normalized VLFM semantic value + lambda_info * normalized ray-cast information gain along the BFS path − lambda_dist * normalized path length (both lambdas 1.0)
Low-level control: a pretrained PointNav policy handles waypoint navigation, as in VLFM

setting.backbone: C-RADIOv4 SO400M with SigLIP2 and SAM3 adaptor heads (frozen), plus a pretrained PointNav policy; DeepSeek-V4-Flash used offline for confuser generation
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (640x480, 79° HFoV, depth 0.5–5 m) + pose relative to start
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 30° / STOP, via a pretrained PointNav policy following frontier waypoints

numbers_note: The paper does not name the splits (val/test) for the three benchmarks; 'val' is an assumption. The real-world results (38/40 success) and the efficiency table (108.63 steps, 24.39 s/episode on the first 100 HM3D-v2 episodes) are not simulator benchmark numbers and are not listed in 'numbers'. The Fig. 1 intro figure and the lambda-ablation figure are graphical only.
results: AECNav gets 84.7 SR / 45.3 SPL on HM3D-v2 (vs TrajRAG 78.1/40.2, ApexNav 76.2/38.0), 51.3/25.9 on MP3D (vs WMNav SR 45.4), and 57.3/30.5 on HM3D-OVON (vs MSGNav 48.3/27.0). It takes 24.39 s and 108.63 steps per episode (VLFM: 53.36 s, 169.43 steps), and reaches 38/40 success on a Unitree Go2 at about 5 Hz.
limitations: Real-world failures came from a target in a corner never seen by the forward-facing camera and from step-budget exhaustion in a large open area; the real-world evaluation is small (40 trials, 4 scenes).

Relies on an LLM to generate confuser categories offline and on many hand-set thresholds and weights (gate, detection, stop, alpha, delta, s_miss); the lambda choice is fixed across datasets and not tuned per dataset.
The efficiency comparison uses only the first 100 HM3D-v2 episodes, and the baselines run under different frameworks (e.g. ApexNav via ROS), so runtimes are not fully controlled.
